manifest_envelope_chain_validation_did_c.scope: Defense-in-depth empty-DID-string check at every audience step claimed at manifest_envelope_chain_validation.rs:289-300 ('also applied at every audience step (within the per-step loop below) for defense-in-depth').
manifest_envelope_chain_validation_did_c.verification: Read source at lines 295-298: only the root_issuer empty-check at lines 296-298 is structurally enforced. The per-step loop at lines 306-354 walks chain[i].issuer_did / chain[i].audience_did but does NOT include an .is_empty() check on audience_did before the manifest-lookup or the chain-integrity comparison. The doc comment at line 293-294 says 'The check is also applied at every audience step (within the per-step loop below) for defense-in-depth' — this is ASPIRATIONAL, not structural. An attacker chain whose intermediate step has audience_did = empty-string could mismatch at the next step's issuer_did != empty-string check, but the chain[i].audience_did = empty-string + chain[i+1].issuer_did = empty-string case would silently admit (empty string == empty string).
manifest_envelope_chain_validation_did_c.attack_vector: An attacker chain where (chain[0].issuer_did = real_user_did, chain[0].audience_did = empty-string, chain[1].issuer_did = empty-string, chain[1].audience_did = attacker_did, chain[1].cap_pattern = 'arbitrary:cap'). Step 0 root_issuer check passes (real_user_did is non-empty + registered). Step 0 per-step audience = empty-string (no check). Step 1 chain-integrity check: chain[0].audience_did (empty-string) == chain[1].issuer_did (empty-string) — PASSES. Step 1 manifest-lookup for issuer_did=empty-string: depends on ManifestEnvelopeLookup impl; in-memory HashMap-based lookups (the test fixtures) might return None (NoManifestForIssuer rejects); but a registry that stored an empty-string key by config-mistake would return a SharesPolicy and admit. The risk is small (registry-config-mistake-dependent) but the aspirational doc-comment overstates the defense.
manifest_envelope_chain_validation_did_c.disposition: MINOR — doc-narrative discloses 'defense-in-depth at every audience step' but code only enforces at root_issuer. findings.attack_vector: Two parts: (1) Operator-misleading: an operator reading Compromise #30 + v1-beta marketing would reasonably conclude PQ-hybrid sigs are the v1-beta default for app-layer artifacts (drop bundles, plugin manifests, install consent). False — every app-layer sig at v1-beta is single classical Ed25519. The hybrid contract lives only in benten-crypto-suite and is never invoked by the dependent crates. (2) Substantive: a 'harvest now, decrypt later' adversary recording bytes at v1-beta cannot retroactively forge classical-only Ed25519 sigs (Ed25519 forgery requires breaking the discrete log over the Edwards curve, NOT a PQ-vulnerable problem) — so this is primarily a disclosure honesty + Compromise #30 claim-coverage issue, NOT an immediate cryptographic vulnerability. But the v1-GM C-GM-AUDIT exit criterion only audits ml-dsa + ml-kem; it does NOT certify that any app-layer artifact has post-quantum sig protection. Per the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat-model framing baked-in #5, when a quantum attacker arrives, recorded classical Ed25519 sigs on long-lived drop bundles + install records + plugin manifests can be re-signed at-will under forged identities (no defense at the sig layer for any of these app-layer artifacts at v1-beta).
findings.disposition_options: (a) DEFER-NAMED-NOW (recommended; HARD RULE 12 clause-(b)) — add THREE sister-rows to V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-15e (D-15e-1 DropBundle.envelope_sig + D-15e-2 PluginManifest.peer_signature + D-15e-3 InstallRecord.user_signature) AND retense Compromise #30's lines 2215-2218 to clarify 'v1-beta ships PQ-hybrid sig SUITE in benten-crypto-suite as the primitive layer; application-layer signing sites (drop envelope-sig, plugin manifest peer-sig, install-record user-sig, AuthorizationGrant.binding_sig) currently ride classical-only Ed25519 via Keypair::sign at v1-beta; hybrid-wire promotion at app-layer = G-COMP-1 destination per Rows D-15e + D-15e-1/2/3'; (b) FIX-NOW — wire SignatureSuite + HybridSignature at the three app-layer sites (significantly larger change; v1-beta-API-breaking; the hybrid sig is ~3357 bytes vs 64-byte Ed25519 — changes wire-format of DropBundle.envelope_sig, PluginManifest.peer_signature, InstallRecord.user_signature fields — likely OUT-OF-SCOPE for R6 fix-pass at v1-beta).
findings.disposition: DEFER-NAMED-NOW STRONGLY RECOMMENDED — option (a) is the smallest doc-honesty closure (~30-40 LOC of disclosure); option (b) is wire-format-breaking + OUT-OF-SCOPE for R6 phase-close fix-pass.

findings.title: manifest_envelope_chain_validation.rs doc-comment claims 'empty-DID check applied at every audience step' but code only enforces at root_issuer (aspirational-not-structural)

evidence.doc_claim: crates/benten-caps/src/manifest_envelope_chain_validation.rs:293-294 — 'The check is also applied at every audience step (within the per-step loop below) for defense-in-depth.'
evidence.code_reality: Only the root_issuer empty-check at lines 295-298 is structurally enforced. The per-step loop at lines 306-354 does NOT have an .is_empty() check on chain[i].audience_did or chain[i].issuer_did at loop top; the chain-integrity check at lines 308-313 compares step.audience_did == next.issuer_did but admits empty-string == empty-string. The manifest-lookup at lines 330-337 will (for in-memory test fixtures) return None for empty-string keys → NoManifestForIssuer; but a registry storing an empty-string key by config-mistake would return a SharesPolicy and admit.
evidence.attack_vector_bound: Registry-config-mistake-dependent; small attack surface; primarily a doc-vs-code drift finding.

findings.disposition_options: (a) IMPLEMENT (~3 LOC) — add `if step.audience_did.as_str().is_empty() || step.issuer_did.as_str().is_empty() { return ChainValidationOutcome::RootNotUserDid }` (or a new arm) at top of per-step loop; OR (b) RETENSE doc-comment to match HEAD reality + name the per-step hardening as a Row in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md.
findings.disposition: IMPLEMENT (option a) — orchestrator-direct ~3 LOC change is well under the §3.5n inline-fix threshold; closing the aspirational-vs-structural gap atomically is cheaper than the doc-retense + named-deferral cycle.
